title: settlement_loop correctness hardening (pre-wiring keystone) — review-team-3 cluster
description: review-team-3 (w96w45naz) confirmed 5 defects in hermes_quant/daemon/settlement_loop.py, the BMA-Beta-auto-learning keystone (ADR-0083). All LATENT (no production caller — daemon/main.py uses construct_realized_outcomes/dispatch_settlement, not join_exit_fills), not Monday-blocking, but must be correct BEFORE wiring into dispatch. (1) HIGH: join_exit_fills reads synthetic schema (rec['side']/['qty']/['asof']) incompatible with the real bus from PaperReactor._record_to_dict (asof_decision/asof_execution, target_position_pct/fill_size_pct, NO side/qty/exec_id) — a real entry+exit pair settles to ([],{}); docstring 'reads the SAME records' is false. Fix: bus->lot adapter (side from sign of target_position_pct/fill_size_pct delta, qty from |delta|, asof from asof_execution); correct docstring; real-_record_to_dict-shaped test. (2) MED: same-asof entry/exit matched in reverse (exec_id lexical tie-break) inverts side+magnitude. Fix: tie-break by positional bus index/proposal lineage, opening before closing. (3) MED: out-of-order carry-in opens a phantom opposing lot, violating one-direction-per-queue. Fix: defer the exit on the lot.asof>asof break instead of opening a residual lot; assert invariant. (4) LOW: mixed tz-aware/naive asof across carry-in raises TypeError; normalize to UTC in _coerce_asof. (5) LOW: compute_horizon_return fee (fees/ep) diverges from join_exit_fills (fees/(ep*qty)) for qty!=1; add qty param. Each fix->adversarial-verify, offline-deterministic, additive (keystone stays unwired), asof-honest.

description: The deterministic gate is the FINAL money-safety authority, and its Rule-1/Rule-2 circuit breakers read drawdown/daily-loss against an inception baseline that drifts away from reality every session. Net effect is fail-OPEN: a profitable-from-inception account can suffer a large intraday or peak-to-trough drawdown without tripping either breaker. Fix: persist a durable peak_equity and a session-anchored daily_open_equity across reconstructions rather than hardcoding initial_cash. || EVIDENCE: VERIFIED hermes_quant/daemon/portfolio_loader.py:85 `daily_open_equity = initial_cash` — never reset to start-of-session equity; Portfolio.daily_loss_pct (protocol.py:313-320) then measures loss-since-inception. While cumulative equity stays above initial_cash, daily_loss_pct clamps to 0 via max(0.0,...) after an intraday drop, so Rule-2 daily_loss_circuit_breaker (default 5%) never trips — fail-open. ; VERIFIED hermes_quant/daemon/portfolio_loader.py:86 `peak_equity = initial_cash` and :167 `peak_equity = max(peak_equity, equity_total)` runs ONCE after the loop, so the returned peak is just max(initial_cash, final_equity); the true rolling peak is lost. An account that hit 130k then fell to 115k reads peak=115k -> drawdown 0 instead of ~11.5%, so Rule-1 drawdown_circuit_breaker (default 15%) can fail to trip. ; Stateless live wiring: daemon/main.py:182-188 calls reconstruct_portfolio fresh each tick passing only initial_cash; no durable peak or session-open equity is threaded in, so both baselines reset to inception every tick. ; Prior review docs/reviews/2026-06-07-quant-deep-review/facet-riskgate.txt:13 audited only the gate's NaN-handling of drawdown_pct/daily_loss_pct, not the upstream baselines — unfiled in cr00-cr19/ra00-ra11. || VERIFIED 2026-06-13: peak_equity/daily_open_equity=initial_cash baselines confirmed, BUT same vestigial daemon/main.py path (ra04). Real fail-open in dead code. The LIVE breaker baseline is the autonomous/cap path, not this reconstructor. Routed to Increment 4. Relabel: not live. || DEFERRED 2026-06-13 (workflow wt13usy0p, orchestrator-verified): the fail-OPEN formula is real (portfolio_loader daily_open_equity/peak_equity hardcoded to initial_cash => Rule-1/Rule-2 measure drawdown since INCEPTION) BUT the loader's Portfolio is NOT wired to the live FINAL-authority gate today: the live autonomous tick feeds risk/gate.py a SYNTHETIC flat portfolio (advisor.py:128-148, 'does NOT read real broker state'); the loader's only live consumer (quant-playbook-weekly) never calls risk/gate.py; settlement_loop's loader-join is a v0.1.2-future comment. Per the safety gradient (when unsure, downgrade): landing a session-anchored daily_open_equity/durable-peak fix detached changes a number NO live gate reads — route it AS PART OF the future gate-wiring increment under its own parity test. (Also gated behind cs14: the loader reads a dead schema today.) || RECONCILE 2026-06-14: STATUS: real fail-OPEN formula, but the loader's Portfolio is NOT wired to the live FINAL-authority gate (the live tick uses a synthetic flat portfolio). DEFERRED to the future gate-wiring increment under its own parity test (landing it detached changes a number no live gate reads). Stays OPEN, gate-wiring-blocked.

title: cs14 latest-target reconstruction: avg_entry_price must come from the OPENING fill (cost basis), not the latest re-target/close fill — else weekly pnl_pct/drawdown is mis-grounded on multi-fill positions
description: NOTED in cs14 Prove §scope: the landed Option-B fix sets avg_entry_price = the LATEST fill's fill_price (the record kept by max asof_execution). For a single-fill position (open==latest, the RED test case) this is correct, but for a multi-fill position (open then re-target/add) the entry BASIS should be the OPENING fill's price, not the latest re-target fill — else pnl_pct=(mark-avg_entry)/avg_entry (weekly:465) and the drawdown are computed against the wrong basis. Compounded by ADR-0070 slippage default-ON (fill_price != decision_price). The cs14 RED test (single fill) cannot catch this. FIX: walk the symbol's admitted fills and pick the OPENING fill's price (or a true cost-basis weighted avg across adds) as avg_entry_price, while keeping LATEST-TARGET for qty/sign. Add a multi-fill (open then re-target) regression case. NEW (cs14 critique, wyq1hyjfh). Distinct from cs14 (which fixed the empty-book) — this refines the entry-basis the now-populated book reports.

title: Weekly loader is a NEW unlisted consumer of the cs15 short-inflated equity_total NAV (if a future increment threads state.db NAV into reconstruct_portfolio instead of initial_cash)
description: FORWARD-GUARD (not active today): cs14's NAV-fraction fallback uses the loader's initial_cash param (default 100_000, the weekly passes no override), NOT state.db equity_total — so it does NOT currently consume the cs15-inflated NAV. But if a FUTURE increment wires a real NAV (state.db cash.equity_total via _account_nav_usd) into the reconstruct_portfolio call to make the fallback qty accurate, it would inherit cs15's short-inflation (equity_total double-counts short legs ~2x|notional|), scaling every reconstructed qty up on a book holding shorts. cs15 enumerated its consumers (admissibility share-conversion + autonomous-tick NAV) but NOT the weekly loader. FIX (when cs15 is fixed AND a real NAV is threaded here): make the cs15-aware choice explicitly + prefer reactor_metadata.quantity (already the cs14 primary). NEW (cs14 critique, wyq1hyjfh). Edge of cs15, not its root.

title: cs14 loader inverse-pooling: portfolio_loader.reconstruct_portfolio absolute-target filter `_record_account(r) in {account_id,'paper-default'}` (set-OR) pools the ENTIRE paper-default book into ANY requested account — the live weekly-exit cron (account_id='alpaca-paper') reconstructs a POOLED book
description: VERIFIED LIVE (orchestrator empirically confirmed on ~/.hermes/quant/executions.jsonl): reconstruct_portfolio('alpaca-paper','equity',bus) returns {AAPL,BA,T} — AAPL+BA are paper-default fills, only T is the real alpaca-paper position. daemon/portfolio_loader.py:118 (the cs14-added absolute-target path, commit 4d5cc42) filters `_record_account(r) in {account_id,'paper-default'}` — a set-OR that admits the synthetic paper-default book (PaperReactor+DeterministicEquityReactor, both resolve to 'paper-default' via _record_account) into ANY requested account. The live consumer scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:326 calls reconstruct_portfolio(account_id='alpaca-paper'), so the admit set is {'alpaca-paper','paper-default'} => the entire paper-default book pools into the alpaca-paper Portfolio. The weekly issues -25% stop / time-exit / LEAPS-dd CLOSE decisions against this pooled book, AND the pooling defeats the shadow-comparison purpose of the deliberately-separate alpaca-paper partition (alpaca_paper.py:1-10). This is the INVERSE of what cs14 fixed: cs14 fixed UNDER-inclusion (dead-schema filter dropped all live records => empty book) and introduced OVER-inclusion (paper-default admitted into every account). ASYMMETRY: the LEGACY int-1 path (portfolio_loader.py:90) is STRICT (`r.get('account_id')==account_id`); only the cs14 absolute path is lax. FIX: scope line 118 to `_record_account(r) == account_id` (resolve the record's account via _record_account, compare for EQUALITY) + add a mixed-account regression test (ask for alpaca-paper, assert paper-default fills excluded). LATENT-magnitude today (1 alpaca_paper record, no cross-account symbol) but the pooling is ACTIVE the moment the alpaca book holds positions alongside a non-empty paper-default book (the documented HERMES_QUANT_ALPACA_PAPER shadow steady-state). Distinct from cs18 (reconstruct_portfolio_state in portfolio/state.py — different reader, autonomous-rail consumer, library-half landed d71a399) and cs16 (closed). NEW (cs18 concurrent critique, workflow ww84qy5yv, orchestrator-verified live). The cs18 fix landed the SAME account-equality pattern in the sibling reader — apply it here too. || ORCHESTRATOR DEEP-DIVE 2026-06-14 (do NOT inline-fix — entangled design question): the naive fix (line 118 `in {account_id,'paper-default'}` -> `== account_id`) is INSUFFICIENT and would swap over-inclusion for UNDER-inclusion. VERIFIED on the live bus: the weekly cron hardcodes account_id='alpaca-paper' (quant-playbook-weekly.py:326) but the REAL managed book is paper-default (10 positions: AAL/AAPL/ASTS/AVGO/BA/CBOE/CDNS/CRM/META/ORCL); alpaca-paper holds only T. So `== account_id` would make the weekly manage ONLY {T} and STOP managing the 10 paper-default positions entirely (it would never stop/take-profit/LEAPS-close AAPL/BA/...). The set-OR was MASKING a deeper question: the weekly is requesting the WRONG account. The fix increment must decide BOTH: (a) tighten the filter to account-EQUALITY (matching cs18's landed pattern + the legacy int-1 path strictness), AND (b) correct the weekly's account request to 'paper-default' (the real managed book) — or justify why it requests alpaca-paper. A Prove stage must confirm which account the weekly SHOULD manage (paper-default = the synthetic live book incl det-equity; alpaca-paper = the shadow-comparison book) before changing either. This is investigate-then-recommend, NOT a one-line patch. || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 99eaff4). Two-part lockstep fix: (1) portfolio_loader.py filter `_record_account(r) == account_id` (account equality — kills the set-OR pooling + the unknown-account sentinel leak; mirrors the operator-approved cs18 sibling + the legacy strict path); (2) both weekly twins request account_id='paper-default' (the REAL managed book) instead of the stale 'alpaca-paper' default the set-OR was masking — justified from ADR-0035 §90-92 + dispatch.py:86 (default PaperReactor->paper-default) + deterministic_equity.py:79 (shares paper-default) + alpaca_paper.py:67 (flag-gated SHADOW) + live reality + git history (alpaca-paper untouched since the weekly's first commit). Empirically verified on the live bus: reconstruct(paper-default)->{AAPL,BA} (real book), reconstruct(alpaca-paper)->{T} (shadow isolated), reconstruct(nonexistent)->{} (no leak). Both halves required in lockstep (equality alone would under-include {AAPL,BA}). Both twins identical; 100-test combined verification green; portfolio_state.py (cs31) untouched. The LAST open P1 of the account-partition strand (cs16/cs18/cs24).

title: ops/scripts/quant-flatten-paper-default.py under-flattens vs the post-cs16 cap view: reads reactor_filter='paper' (lines 77,157) while the autonomous rail+caps gate now read reactor_filter=None — the headroom-recovery tool leaves det-equity/alpaca positions open and reports a false 'flat'
description: VERIFIED: ops/scripts/quant-flatten-paper-default.py:77 `ps=reconstruct_portfolio_state(BUS)  # reactor_filter='paper' (cap view)` and :157 (post-flatten verify) both read the default 'paper' filter. The docstring (lines 1-19) states it closes 'every OPEN position in the view the ADR-0087 portfolio cap and the autonomous tick actually read' — TRUE pre-cs16. cs16 (commit 2f1a280) changed autonomous.py rail+caps gate to reactor_filter=None (whole book: paper + deterministic-equity + alpaca_paper); the flatten op-script was NOT updated. title: Weekly find_entry_record/infer_play_tag accept ONLY a 'buy' opening leg, so every SHORT dead-ends at the entry-is-None ERROR branch BEFORE cs20's sign-aware exit math runs — cs20 is latent on shorts
description: VERIFIED at scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:296 (+ ops twin): find_entry_record requires `_rec_side(rec) == "buy"`. _rec_side (cs17, lines 238) maps a negative target_position_pct to side 'sell', so a SHORT's opening leg is a 'sell' => find_entry_record returns None for every short, and infer_play_tag (line 279 `if _rec_side(rec) != "buy": continue`) skips the short's opening leg too. In run_weekly (lines 491-506): entry=find_entry_record(...); if entry is None: log action='ERROR' ('no opening execution found for held position') and continue. So the exit-rule block (days_held + mark fetch + the just-landed cs20 sign-aware compute_pnl_drawdown -> decide_swing/decide_leaps CLOSE decisions) is UNREACHABLE for any short. NET on the short-dominated live book: cs14 repopulates qty<0 shorts, cs20 makes the math sign-correct, but the weekly STILL drops every short at this buy-only gate, logging a spurious ERROR and never running the stop/3xATR-TP/LEAPS -25% close on a real short. cs20's correctness is LATENT until this gate accepts a short's opening sell leg. FIX: recognize the OPENING leg by position-sign DIRECTION (the opening leg shares the sign of the held position; a short opens with a sell), not =="buy"; keep the long path byte-identical; apply to BOTH twins. DISTINCT: cs14=loader reconstruction reachability; cs20=the math (now sign-aware, unreached on shorts); cs21=_fire_equity_close direction/signature (downstream of the close decision); cs22=avg_entry cost-basis (assumes an entry WAS found — never is, for a short). This is the find_entry_record side-filter INSIDE the weekly. NEW (cs20 concurrent critique, workflow ww00ffmsg, orchestrator-verified at :296). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 0f60895). Both weekly helpers gained a trailing position_qty=0.0 + desired_side='sell' if qty<0 else 'buy', gating on _rec_side==desired_side; run_weekly threads pos.qty. Long byte-identical (qty>=0->'buy'); legacy explicit-side records still match; account_id line (cs24) untouched; twins identical; 55-test combined verification green. The cs14->cs26->cs20 short chain is now connected: a held short finds its sell opening leg and REACHES the sign-aware exit math. RESIDUAL (filed): cs27 (P1 find_entry_record FIRST-match days_held inflation on re-opened shorts) + cs28 (P2 oldest-vs-newest leg asymmetry) — cs26 fixed the SIDE gate, not the WHICH-leg semantics.

title: Weekly find_entry_record FIRST-match inflates days_held on re-opened/multi-fill shorts -> spurious armed swing-stop CLOSE on a freshly re-entered position
description: VERIFIED + reproduced (cs26 critique). The loader's absolute-target path keeps ONLY the LATEST record per asset (daemon/portfolio_loader.py:245-255, max asof_execution; qty/sign/avg_entry from the latest) with NO partial/flip guard on the abs path (the NotImplementedError guard is only the legacy int-1 loop 160-173), so re-opens/flips fold silently. But find_entry_record (scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:293-298 + ops twin, now sign-aware post-cs26) returns the FIRST file-order sign-matching record. For a short re-opened after a flat (BA: -0.2@2026-01-05, 0.0@2026-03-01, -0.2@2026-06-08; loader's current short is 5 days old) find_entry_record returns the 2026-01-05 leg -> days_held=159. The armed swing stop fires on (days_held>60 AND pnl_pct<0) at decide_swing (weekly:163); a re-opened LOSING short (cs20 makes pnl_pct<0 reachable, cs26 makes the path reachable) with stale days_held=159 triggers a REAL armed CLOSE (_fire_equity_close, line 603) on a 5-day-old position. Also hits multi-fill short adds (AVGO -0.1@02-01 then -0.2@06-09 -> days_held=132 off the original). FIX: find_entry_record must select the CURRENT position's opening leg = the most-recent sign-matching record at/after the last flat-or-flip transition (mirroring the loader's latest-target leg), not the first-ever file-order match. Money-software, live exit cron (DRY-RUN default). NOT cs26 (side gate, done) / NOT cs22 (avg_entry cost-basis in loader) / NOT cs00 (legacy realized-PnL sign). NEW (cs26 concurrent critique, workflow w3s7ygq7b, orchestrator-verified). Note: cs26's own Prove flagged this 'first-same-sign over-ages, never under-ages, symmetric with the pre-cs26 long residual' and scoped it OUT — this seed is the fix. || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit d6c8b11). _establishing_leg helper anchors find_entry_record/infer_play_tag on the first fill of the held sign in the current run (bounded by the last flat/flip), so days_held reads age from when the current run opened. Re-opened short independently re-derived: days_held 160->6, armed 60d swing-stop now HOLDs on a fresh re-open. Single-fill long byte-identical; both twins identical; 57-test combined verification green.

title: Weekly find_entry_record (FIRST/oldest leg) and infer_play_tag (reversed/newest leg) select DIFFERENT entry legs for multi-fill positions -> days_held grounded on a different leg than play/qty/avg_entry
description: VERIFIED + reproduced (cs26 critique). Even after cs26 made both helpers sign-aware, they keep divergent traversal: find_entry_record uses FIRST file-order match (weekly:295), infer_play_tag uses reversed()=most-recent (weekly:276), and the loader uses LATEST-TARGET (portfolio_loader.py:245-255). For any asset with 2+ same-direction fills the three anchor to different records: AVGO short (-0.1@2026-02-01, -0.2@2026-06-09) -> find_entry_record=2026-02-01 (days_held source), infer_play_tag=2026-06-09 (play source), loader qty/avg_entry=2026-06-09. days_held is the lone metric anchored to the OLDEST leg while play classification + qty/basis come from the NEWEST -> a structurally inconsistent position-management decision (swing-vs-leaps routing + qty from one leg, age from another). Distinct from cs27 (re-opened-short days_held INFLATION across a flat): this is the silent oldest-vs-newest leg ASYMMETRY across the two readers even for a never-closed add. NOT cs22 (cost-basis in loader). FIX: unify the entry leg all three (find_entry_record, infer_play_tag, loader) agree on — likely the leg that established the current position per cs27. Best fixed TOGETHER with cs27 (same root: 'which leg is the entry for a multi-fill position'). NEW (cs26 concurrent critique, workflow w3s7ygq7b). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit d6c8b11, with cs27 — same root). find_entry_record + infer_play_tag now BOTH delegate to _establishing_leg, so days_held/play/loader agree on ONE leg (the first-of-current-run). Multi-fill add (AVGO -0.1@02-01, -0.2@06-09) anchors both readers on the 02-01 establishing leg (play='leaps'), not the split oldest/newest.

title: Weekly 3xATR swing take-profit uses CURRENT ATR wired into the AT-ENTRY field (ADR-0035 §98 violation): fetch_mark_atr computes ATR over a 60d window ending TODAY, run_weekly feeds it to SwingContext.atr14_at_entry_pct
description: VERIFIED genuinely-new (cs27 critique). ADR-0035 §98 requires the take-profit threshold to use ATR-14_AT_ENTRY; the dataclass field encodes it (SwingContext.atr14_at_entry_pct, scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:145) and decide_swing's TP rule is tp_threshold = SWING_TP_ATR_MULT * ctx.atr14_at_entry_pct (weekly:168-169). BUT fetch_mark_atr (weekly:393-400) computes the CURRENT ATR: t.history(period='60d') ends TODAY, close=h['Close'].iloc[-1] (today's close), atr=tr.tail(14).mean(); its own docstring says 'atr14_pct_at_recent_close' (weekly:381). run_weekly wires this CURRENT atr into the AT-ENTRY field: mark, atr_pct = fetch_mark_atr(asset) (weekly:539) -> decide_swing(SwingContext(..., atr14_at_entry_pct=atr_pct or 0.0)) (weekly:573). IMPACT: the 3xATR take-profit fires against TODAY's vol regime, not entry-time — too early if vol fell since entry (threshold shrank), too late if vol spiked. ORTHOGONAL to cs27/cs28 (which fix WHICH leg supplies days_held/play): even with the correct establishing leg, the ATR still comes from today's window. SHORT-SPECIFIC 2nd-order (cs20 interaction): for a short pnl_pct=(avg_entry-mark)/avg_entry but atr_pct=atr/close uses the CURRENT mark as denominator — as a short profits (mark falls) the atr_pct denominator shrinks, inflating the TP threshold, making a deeply-profitable short HARDER to take-profit. FIX: compute ATR over the window ENDING at the establishing-leg date (now available post-cs27) and divide by the entry-date close, not today's. BEST LANDED NOW (cs27 made the establishing-leg date reliably available). Standing bug since file creation. DRY-RUN default. NEW (cs27 concurrent critique, workflow waf19tg7q, orchestrator-verified). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 90faa28). fetch_mark_atr gained optional entry_date: ATR-14 window ending at the cs27 establishing-leg date + entry-date close denominator (ADR-0035 §98), removing both the regime drift and the cs20 short atr/mark denominator drift. entry_date=None byte-identical; layered no-fabrication fallback to recent-ATR + journal atr_basis marker. Stable-vol single-fill-long TP ~unchanged; both twins identical; 55-test combined verification green.

title: Weekly days_between_iso guards only `except ValueError`, so a non-str asof_execution/asof (numeric epoch / null / pd.Timestamp leak) raises uncaught AttributeError/TypeError, killing the per-asset loop / whole run
description: VERIFIED at scripts/quant-playbook-weekly.py:313-322. days_between_iso does `s = asof_iso.replace('Z','+00:00')` then datetime.fromisoformat(s), wrapped ONLY by `except ValueError: return 0`. If asof_iso is not a str, .replace raises AttributeError (numeric/None) or fromisoformat raises TypeError — neither caught. Caller (weekly:535-536) passes entry.get('asof_execution') or entry.get('asof',''). asof_execution is typed str (react/base.py:61) so the LIVE bus is safe TODAY; the docstring claims 'Robust to ISO with or without Z' but it is NOT robust to non-str input. A malformed/legacy/settlement record with a numeric or null asof_execution would raise an uncaught exception that propagates out of the per-asset loop -> main()'s catch-all logs weekly_uncaught_exception and returns 1 -> NO decisions for the WHOLE run (silence-by-default hides it). P3: defensive-only, low probability given typed producers, no money-state corruption — but a single bad bus line silently disables the entire weekly rebalance. FIX: widen to `except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError)` or coerce str(asof_iso) before parsing. NOT cs27/cs28. NEW (cs27 concurrent critique, workflow waf19tg7q). Cheap to fold into the cs29 increment (same file). || RESOLVED-MERGED 2026-06-14 (commit 90faa28, with cs29). days_between_iso widened to `except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError): return 0` — a non-str asof now degrades that position to days_held=0 instead of aborting the whole weekly run via main's catch-all. str-ISO happy path byte-identical.

title: get_marked_equity treats true-shares/contract positions as NAV-fractions: MTM off by nav_ref (and the option contract-multiplier) — orphaned read-time API, no live caller
description: VERIFIED (cs15 critique): portfolio_state.py:954 get_marked_equity computes unrealized_i = pos.quantity * nav_ref * (mark/avg_entry - 1.0), hardcoding the NAV-FRACTION basis (docstring :926). But the two write folds (_apply_execution_unsafe :639-662, _replay_record :1137-1149) branch on reactor_metadata.quantity (leg_quantity): multi-leg/Alpaca positions persist quantity in REAL SHARES/CONTRACTS (the cr00/cr01 unit-basis split), NOT a NAV fraction. get_marked_equity does NOT branch on unit. Traced: long 50sh @100, mark 110, nav_ref 100000 -> current 50*100000*(110/100-1)=500,000 vs correct real-shares MTM 50*(110-100)=500 (off by ~nav_ref, ~1000x here); us_option ALSO omits _CONTRACT_MULTIPLIER (another 100x). DISTINCT from cs15 (equity_total cost-basis SIGN; the get_marked_equity SHORT SIGN is verified CORRECT: short -0.2@100 -> mark 90 = +2000) and from cr00/cr01 (loader/cap-clip basis). P2 not P1: get_marked_equity has NO live production caller (only a comment at cli/status.py:595 + a do-NOT-wire note at react/paper.py:123) — an orphaned-but-built MTM instrument; the unit bug bleeds only once a true-shares book is fed to a WIRED marked-report surface. FIX: branch the MTM math on the same leg_quantity/true-unit predicate the folds use (real-shares: quantity*(mark-entry)*contract_multiplier; NAV-fraction: keep quantity*nav_ref*(mark/entry-1)), preserving the short sign. NEW (cs15 concurrent critique, workflow w2znwt0w7). Check orphan-status (is it ever wired?) before building — same orphaned-instrument lesson. || ANALYSIS DONE, MERGE SCOPE-REJECTED 2026-06-14 (workflow wvmfbf83f). A B2 workflow PROVED the read-time unit is not recoverable without persistence (see cs33) and IMPLEMENTED the correct fix (qty_unit column + idempotent ALTER TABLE migration + both write folds stamp it + branched MTM; short sign preserved; nav-fraction byte-identical; 21+70 tests green). The orchestrator REJECTED the merge on SCOPE: get_marked_equity is ORPHANED (no live caller), so a live state.db SCHEMA MIGRATION + relaxing the restate read-only DDL guarantee to fix a bug nothing consumes is the wrong trade. Validated implementation + RED tests preserved at docs/design/2026-06-14-cs31-marked-equity-unit-analysis.md. RE-SCOPE: land cs31 (MTM branch) + cs33 (qty_unit schema column) TOGETHER as a dedicated, separately-reviewed increment WHEN get_marked_equity is wired to a live marked-report surface OR an operator approves the schema migration on its own merits. Stays OPEN (re-scoped, not abandoned). The correctness analysis is the durable deliverable; the live-money schema change is deferred to a justified trigger.

title: get_marked_equity equity_basis flag can never report 'mark' when an invalid-avg position is present (label artifact, not a money number)
description: VERIFIED (cs15 critique): portfolio_state.py:947 skips positions with avg_entry_price<=0 via `continue` (so they never increment n_marked), but :961 sets n_positions = len(positions) INCLUDING the skipped one. A book with one bad-avg position can therefore never satisfy n_marked==n_positions, so equity_basis collapses to 'mixed' even when every VALID position is marked. Affects only the reporting-flag label (MarkedEquity.equity_basis), NOT marked_equity/total_unrealized money figures. Low-stakes; fold into the cs31 unit-fix (same function) or skip. NOT cs15/cr00/cr01. NEW (cs15 concurrent critique, workflow w2znwt0w7). || ANALYSIS DONE, BUNDLED-WITH-cs31 2026-06-14 (workflow wvmfbf83f). The n_positions-counts-skipped-rows label fix (use n_considered as the denominator) was implemented + tested green in the same workflow, but rides the same orphaned-get_marked_equity merge the orchestrator scope-rejected (it edits the same function). Re-scoped to land WITH cs31/cs33 when get_marked_equity is wired/approved. Trivial (reporting-label only, no money figure); captured in docs/design/2026-06-14-cs31-marked-equity-unit-analysis.md.

title: get_marked_equity cannot recover position UNIT at read time (positions table persists no unit flag) — a true-shares row and a NAV-fraction row are byte-identical, so the cs31 MTM fix needs a schema column, NOT a read-time re-derivation
description: VERIFIED (cs31 Prove + critique, analysis preserved at docs/design/2026-06-14-cs31-marked-equity-unit-analysis.md): the positions table schema (portfolio_state.py:175-183) stores ONLY {account_id, asset_class, symbol, quantity, avg_entry_price, last_update_at} — NO unit flag. The write folds discriminate real-shares vs NAV-fraction by reactor_metadata.quantity PRESENCE at write time (_apply_execution_unsafe :681-683 leg_quantity), but that signal is CONSUMED and never persisted; only the resulting quantity lands in the row. asset_class does NOT discriminate (multileg/alpaca write real-shares rows with asset_class='equity', same as the legacy NAV-fraction paper path). So get_marked_equity literally cannot branch on the write-fold unit predicate — a 50-share equity long and a 0.5 NAV-fraction equity long are indistinguishable rows. The honest fix REQUIRES persistence (a qty_unit column + a migration on the live state.db) OR a caller-supplied unit policy — NOT a read-time heuristic. DISPOSITION 2026-06-14: a cs31 workflow PROVED + IMPLEMENTED exactly this (qty_unit column + idempotent ALTER TABLE + both write folds stamp it + branched MTM), all tests green — BUT the orchestrator REJECTED the merge: get_marked_equity is ORPHANED (no live caller), so paying a live money-state SCHEMA MIGRATION + relaxing the restate read-only DDL guarantee (test_restate_does_not_mutate_state_db) to fix a bug nothing consumes is the wrong trade. The schema migration is a real money-state change that deserves its own reviewed increment, NOT a rider on an orphaned read-API fix. ROUTE: fix cs31's MTM (cs31 stays open) TOGETHER with this schema column AS A DEDICATED increment WHEN get_marked_equity is actually wired to a live marked-report surface (or when an operator approves the schema migration on its own merits). The validated implementation + RED tests are captured in the design doc for fast re-land. NEW (cs31 concurrent critique, workflow wvmfbf83f, orchestrator scope-rejected the merge).

title: get_marked_equity does not validate mark finiteness/positivity: a NaN mark NaNs the whole account equity snapshot; a 0/negative mark books a >=100% phantom loss
description: VERIFIED (cs31 critique): portfolio_state.py:996-1000 does mark = mark_prices.get(pos.symbol); if mark is not None: unrealized = quantity*nav_ref*(mark/avg_entry-1.0). ONLY `is not None` is checked — no isfinite/positivity guard. A NaN mark -> unrealized NaN -> total_unrealized NaN -> marked_equity NaN (one bad symbol poisons the WHOLE account equity figure) while n_marked still increments (so equity_basis can read 'mark' on a NaN book). A 0.0 mark -> mark/entry-1 = -1 -> full -100% on that leg; negative -> >100% loss. DISTINCT from cr05 (which rejects zero/negative DECISION price in the WRITE/PaperReactor path; this is the READ-path injected MARK, not covered by cr05's guard). Orphaned read-time API (no live caller) so LATENT, but bleeds the instant a marked-report surface feeds a mark dict that can contain NaN/0/neg (e.g. a yfinance fetch miss returning NaN).
